## Problem
`LaserQuarryBlockEntity.tick` checks `phaseRunner.isFinished()` (pre-refactor: `entity.finished`) and returns early *before* resetting `consumedEnergyThisTick`. If the quarry was actively consuming energy on the tick it finished, the flag remains true forever — its public getter is read by the client renderer (LED indicator), so the indicator may stay "lit" indefinitely after the quarry is done.

## Location
`common/src/main/java/com/logistics/automation/laserquarry/entity/LaserQuarryBlockEntity.java:122-145` (post-refactor)
`common/src/main/java/com/logistics/automation/laserquarry/entity/LaserQuarryBlockEntity.java:150-163` (pre-refactor on `mc/26.1`)

```java
if (entity.phaseRunner.isFinished()) {
    return;   // <-- consumedEnergyThisTick not cleared
}
// ...later in the same method...
entity.consumedEnergyThisTick = false;
```

## Suggested fix
Reset `consumedEnergyThisTick = false` (and trigger a final sync if it changed) before the `isFinished` early return so the LED state is consistent post-finish. Add a regression test that runs the BE for one extra tick after `phaseRunner.setFinished(true)` (or equivalent) and asserts the flag transitions to false.

## History
Surfaced in PR #406 review. Pre-existing on `mc/26.1`, `mc/1.21.11`, and `mc/1.21.1` — the refactor PR is pure extraction, so the fix was deferred to its own PR for traceability and cross-branch cherry-picks.

Runtime config values are parsed and assigned directly without validation. Invalid values such as negative speeds, negative energy multipliers, NaN, Infinity, or zero/negative scan rates can reach physics, energy, and quarry logic.

## Summary
EnergyComponent does not guard against non-positive transfer requests or invalid configured limits/capacity. Negative input or negative config-derived values can make insert/extract return negative amounts, violating normal energy storage semantics.

## Evidence
- common/src/main/java/com/logistics/core/lib/energy/EnergyComponent.java:36 calculates accepted with Math.min(maxAmount, ...), with no maxAmount <= 0 guard.
- common/src/main/java/com/logistics/core/lib/energy/EnergyComponent.java:47 does the same for extraction.
- Config-derived values such as quarry energy capacity/input can become negative if config accepts negative multipliers.

## Suggested fix
Clamp transfer requests and derived values to non-negative values. insert/extract should immediately return 0 for maxAmount <= 0, negative capacity should be treated as 0, and maxInsert/maxExtract should not allow negative effective transfer amounts.

Add EnergyComponent tests for negative maxAmount, zero/negative limits, and negative dynamic capacity suppliers.

## Summary
Dropped or discarded logistics items currently call the same delivery path as successful inventory insertion. That can mark jobs complete even though the requested items never reached the destination inventory.

## Evidence
- common/src/main/java/com/logistics/pipe/runtime/PipeRuntime.java:257 calls network.notifyDelivery before dropping a routed item.
- common/src/main/java/com/logistics/pipe/runtime/PipeRuntime.java:441 does the same in notifyDropAndDrop.

- common/src/main/java/com/logistics/pipe/network/NetworkJob.java:75 records this as delivery and may transition the job to COMPLETE.

Split the network API into separate success and failure/accounting paths, for example recordDelivery(...) for real inventory arrival and releaseOutstanding(...) or recordLoss(...) for failed extraction/drop/discard paths. Dropped items should decrement outstanding requester accounting without incrementing deliveredAmount or completing the job.

Add a focused regression test for tracked TravelingItem drop/failure paths to verify ordered counts are released but NetworkJob deliveredAmount is not incremented.

## Background

A recent incident exposed a gap in CI coverage: missing `META-INF/services/` registration files caused the mod to fail at runtime (ServiceLoader throws on startup), but all CI checks passed because nothing exercises the JVM after a clean checkout.

## Goal

Build a test suite that:
- Tests all business logic in `common` with no dependency on Fabric API or NeoForge
- Uses Minecraft classes as a test dependency (acceptable trade-off for now)
- Keeps `fabric`/`neoforge` test scope limited to unit tests of their thin adapter implementations

## Proposed Structure

```
common/src/test/java/        # JUnit, MC as compile dep, no Fabric/NeoForge
fabric/src/test/java/        # Unit tests for Fabric adapters (FabricFuelHelper, etc.)
neoforge/src/test/java/      # Unit tests for NeoForge adapters
```

### common tests
- Shared base class calls `Bootstrap.bootStrap()` in `@BeforeAll` to initialize MC registries
- Test business logic directly: pipe routing, engine fuel consumption, network graph, etc.
- No loader APIs — if Fabric leaks into common, it fails to compile here (free architectural guard)

### fabric / neoforge tests
- Plain JUnit where possible, but likely will need platform tools (like `@GameTest`)
- Verify ServiceLoader registrations are present: `ServiceLoader.load(FuelHelper.class).findFirst().orElseThrow()`
- Test adapter correctness: given a known item, does `FabricFuelHelper.checkBurnDuration()` return the expected value?

## Immediate Win

The ServiceLoader smoke test in `fabric` and `neoforge` would have caught the missing `META-INF/services/` files that broke the mc/26.1 snapshot release. This is the first thing to implement.

## Notes

- `@GameTest` is intentionally avoided — game tests are loader-specific and the goal is loader-agnostic test coverage
- `Bootstrap.bootStrap()` is slow but a one-time cost per test run; acceptable for now
- Future direction: push MC types to the edges (domain types in common, MC conversion at adapter boundary) to remove the Bootstrap dependency entirely

## Overview

All client-side code currently lives in `fabric/src/client/`. To support NeoForge (and future loaders), the vanilla-compatible portions need to move to `common/src/client/` and the loader-specific parts need abstraction layers — the same pattern used on the server side.

## What's vanilla-compatible (move to `common/src/client/`)

**Screens — pure vanilla, zero loader dependencies:**
- All pipe screens: `RequesterScreen`, `SupplierScreen`, `ProviderScreen`, `SinkScreen`, `CraftingScreen`, `ProcessScreen`, `SatelliteScreen`, `ChassisScreen`, `ItemFilterScreen`, `AdvancedExtractorScreen`, `ModSinkScreen` — plus `widget/` subdirectory
- `power/screen/StirlingEngineScreen.java`
- `automation/kiln/KilnScreen.java` + `KilnRecipeBookComponent.java`
- `core/macerator/MaceratorScreen.java` + `MaceratorRecipeBookComponent.java`
- JEI integration: `core/macerator/jei/` (JEI is loader-agnostic)

**Bootstrap SPI — vanilla ServiceLoader, no Fabric API:**
- `core/bootstrap/ClientDomainBootstrap.java`
- `core/bootstrap/ClientDomainBootstraps.java`
- `core/bootstrap/LogisticsClientBootstrap.java`

## What needs abstraction before it can be shared

### Client networking

Currently `ClientPlayNetworking` is used in two places:

1. **Receiving packets** — `ClientPlayNetworking.registerGlobalReceiver()` in `LogisticsPipeClient.registerPacketReceivers()`
2. **Sending packets** — `ClientPlayNetworking.send()` in `RequesterScreen`, `ChassisScreen`

Fix: introduce `ClientNetworking` SPI in `core.lib.platform` (same Pattern A shape as `ServerNetworking` from #352). Fabric wires `ClientPlayNetworking`; NeoForge wires its equivalent.

### Model loading

~80 extra models are registered across all domain clients via Fabric's `ExtraModelKey` + `ModelLoadingPlugin`. Renderers access them by casting to `FabricModelManager`. This is the deepest Fabric dependency in the client layer.

Fix: introduce a `ClientModelRegistry` SPI (Pattern A — ServiceLoader). Fabric provides an `ExtraModelKey`-backed implementation; NeoForge provides its own. Renderers call `ClientModelRegistry.INSTANCE.get(id)` instead of casting `FabricModelManager` directly.

## What stays loader-specific

- `LogisticsModClient` — must implement `ClientModInitializer` (Fabric) or equivalent (NeoForge)
- Domain client bootstraps (`LogisticsPipeClient`, `LogisticsPowerClient`, etc.) — register models, hook events, wire packet receivers; each loader has its own thin version that calls the common abstractions

## Dependency order

```
1. Create common/src/client/ directory structure
2. Move screens + bootstrap SPI (no-risk, pure vanilla, no code changes)
3. Add ClientNetworking SPI + Fabric impl → replace ClientPlayNetworking calls in screens
4. Add ClientModelRegistry SPI + Fabric impl → replace ExtraModelKey / FabricModelManager in domain clients
5. Write NeoForge client bootstrap implementations using the same SPIs
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `common/src/client/` exists and contains all vanilla-compatible screens and bootstrap SPI
- `fabric/src/client/` domain clients are thin wrappers that call common abstractions
- No `net.fabricmc.*` imports in `common/src/client/`
- `neoforge/src/client/` has parallel domain client implementations using the same SPIs
- All 69 Fabric game tests continue to pass

## Problem

`LogisticsPower.java` registers the Stirling Engine menu using Fabric's `ExtendedMenuType`, which sends extra data from server to client when the menu is opened. This is in `common/`.

## Research findings

Both Fabric and NeoForge support extended menu data but via different mechanisms:

- **Fabric:** `ExtendedMenuType` + `ExtendedMenuProvider` — extra data written to a `PacketByteBuf` on the server and read in the menu constructor client-side.
- **NeoForge:** `IContainerFactory` — menu constructor receives an `IMenuType` with a factory that reads from a `FriendlyByteBuf`.

The menu *logic* (slots, data slots, container sync) is vanilla and belongs in `common/`. Only the type registration and the extra-data wiring are loader-specific.

**Recommended approach:**

1. Keep the `AbstractContainerMenu` subclass in `common/` — it reads its extra state from a `FriendlyByteBuf` in its constructor (this is vanilla-compatible).
2. Move `ExtendedMenuType` creation to `fabric/`.
3. For NeoForge, create equivalent `IContainerFactory`-based registration in `neoforge/`.
4. No shared interface needed — the constructor signature is sufficient contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- `LogisticsPower.java` in `common/` has no `ExtendedMenuType` import
- Stirling Engine menu opens and syncs correctly (fuel level, energy) on Fabric

## Problem

`EnergyComponent` extends Team Reborn's `SimpleEnergyStorage`, coupling it to a Fabric-only energy API. It is used throughout `common/` by engines, cables, the quarry, and the kiln.

## Scope

Files that directly use Team Reborn energy types in `common/`:

- `core/lib/energy/EnergyComponent.java` — extends `SimpleEnergyStorage`
- `core/lib/block/capability/HasEnergyStorage.java` — return type is `team.reborn.energy.api.EnergyStorage`
- `core/lib/power/EnergyDemandProvider.java` — return type check
- `power/block/entity/CreativeSinkBlockEntity.java`
- `power/cable/CableBlockEntity.java`, `CableNetwork.java`
- `power/engine/block/entity/RedstoneEngineBlockEntity.java`, `StirlingEngineBlockEntity.java`
- `automation/kiln/KilnBlockEntity.java`
- `automation/laserquarry/entity/LaserQuarryBlockEntity.java`

## Research findings

Team Reborn Energy (Fabric) and NeoForge Energy share the same conceptual API — insert, extract, getAmount, getCapacity — but differ in:

1. **Transaction system:** TRE uses `TransactionContext`; NeoForge Energy uses no transactions (simulate flag instead).
2. **Registration:** TRE uses `BlockApiLookup`; NeoForge uses `ICapabilityProvider`.

**Recommended contract:**

```java
// common/ — no loader imports
public interface IEnergyStorage {
    long insert(long maxAmount, boolean simulate);
    long extract(long maxAmount, boolean simulate);
    long getAmount();
    long getCapacity();
    default boolean canInsert() { return true; }
    default boolean canExtract() { return true; }
}
```

`EnergyComponent` moves to `fabric/` and adapts between `IEnergyStorage` and Team Reborn's `SimpleEnergyStorage`. Block entities in `common/` hold `IEnergyStorage` fields; the Fabric layer wires up the TRE lookup using the wrapped instance.

**Note:** `TransactionContext` parameters on `insert()`/`extract()` disappear from `common/` — only the Fabric wrapper sees them. This simplifies most block entity code significantly.

## Acceptance criteria

- `common/` has no `team.reborn.*` imports
- `HasEnergyStorage` returns `IEnergyStorage`
- All engines, cables, quarry, and kiln work correctly on Fabric
- `IEnergyStorage` is documented as the extension point for loader implementations
payload.title: Define IEnergyStorage contract and move EnergyComponent to fabric/

## Problem

`MaceratorRecipeManager.java` in `common/` registers itself as a resource reload listener using Fabric's `ResourceLoader` API:

```java
import net.fabricmc.fabric.api.resource.ResourceLoader;
// ...
ResourceLoader.get(PackType.SERVER_DATA).registerReloadListener(this);
```

## Research findings

Both loaders support resource reload listeners but via different registration mechanisms:

- **Fabric:** `ResourceLoader.get(type).registerReloadListener(listener)` at init time
- **NeoForge:** `AddReloadListenerEvent` fired during data pack setup

The listener *implementation* (reading JSON files, caching recipes) is entirely vanilla and belongs in `common/`. Only the *registration call* is loader-specific.

**Recommended approach:**

1. Keep `MaceratorRecipeManager` in `common/` — its reload logic uses only vanilla `ResourceManager` / `CompletableFuture`.
2. Create a simple registration hook: expose a static `MaceratorRecipeManager.getInstance()` and call `.registerReloadListener(instance)` from the Fabric entry point.
3. For NeoForge: subscribe to `AddReloadListenerEvent` and add the same instance.

No interface needed between loaders — the listener class is vanilla, only the registration point differs.

## Acceptance criteria

- `common/` has no `net.fabricmc.fabric.api.resource.*` imports
- Macerator recipes reload correctly when resource packs change on Fabric

## Problem

Four packet classes in `common/` contain static `register()` methods that call Fabric's `PayloadTypeRegistry` and `ServerPlayNetworking` directly.

## Files affected

- `pipe/network/packet/SetSatelliteIdPacket.java`
- `pipe/network/packet/RequestItemPacket.java`
- `pipe/network/packet/OpenChassisSlotPacket.java`
- `pipe/network/packet/SyncRequesterInventoryPacket.java`

## Research findings

The packet *data* (fields + codec) is vanilla — perfectly fine in `common/`. Only the `register()` call is Fabric-specific.

**Recommended approach:**

1. Keep packet payload classes in `common/` — they are just data + codec, no Fabric types in the class body after this change.
2. Delete the static `register()` method from each class.
3. In `fabric/`, create a `PacketRegistrar` (or inline in the Fabric entry point) that calls `PayloadTypeRegistry` and `ServerPlayNetworking.registerGlobalReceiver()` directly.
4. For NeoForge: create equivalent registration in `neoforge/` when needed (NeoForge uses `RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent`).

This is the cleanest split: common = what a packet contains, fabric = how to send/receive it.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `net.fabricmc.fabric.api.networking.*` imports in `common/`
- Packet classes in `common/` contain only fields, codec, and `CustomPacketPayload.Type` ID
- Registration wired in `fabric/` entry point; behaviour unchanged

## Problem

`common/` contains Fabric's `BlockApiLookup` / `registerFallback` calls, which are purely Fabric-specific capability plumbing.

## Files affected

| File | Fabric API used |
|------|----------------|
| `core/lib/block/lookup/ItemStorageAccess.java` | `ItemStorage.SIDED.registerFallback()` |
| `core/lib/block/lookup/EnergyStorageAccess.java` | `EnergyStorage.SIDED.registerFallback()` |
| `core/lib/block/lookup/FluidStorageAccess.java` | `FluidStorage.SIDED.registerFallback()` |
| `core/lib/pipe/PipeConnectionRegistry.java` | `BlockApiLookup` |

## Research findings

These files are Fabric's "capability system" — they teach Fabric which blocks expose which APIs. NeoForge has an entirely different capability system (`ICapabilityProvider`, `RegisterCapabilitiesEvent`).

**Recommended approach:** Move all four files to `fabric/src/main/java/.../` unchanged. When NeoForge support is needed, create parallel NeoForge capability registration in `neoforge/`. No shared interface is useful here — the registration shape is completely different between loaders.

The lookup *callers* (e.g. `MinecraftWorldView` reading from neighbouring block entities) will need a separate abstraction tracked in the item/energy storage issues.

## Acceptance criteria

- `common/` has no `BlockApiLookup` imports
- `ItemStorageAccess`, `EnergyStorageAccess`, `FluidStorageAccess`, `PipeConnectionRegistry` live in `fabric/`
- All four are called from the Fabric entry point; Fabric behaviour unchanged

## Problem

Several files in `common/` register Fabric-specific lifecycle and game events directly, making them uncompilable by NeoForge.

## Files affected

| File | Fabric API used |
|------|----------------|
| `core/LogisticsCommands.java` | `CommandRegistrationCallback` |
| `core/network/NetworkTickHandler.java` | `ServerTickEvents`, `ServerLevelEvents` |
| `core/loot/ChestLootModifier.java` | `LootTableEvents` |
| `LogisticsAutomation.java` | `ServerLevelEvents` (quarry cleanup) |

## Research findings

These files have **zero shared logic** between loaders — they are 100% registration glue. NeoForge equivalents:

- `CommandRegistrationCallback` → `RegisterCommandsEvent`
- `ServerTickEvents` → `TickEvent.ServerTickEvent`
- `ServerLevelEvents` → `LevelEvent.Load` / `LevelEvent.Unload`
- `LootTableEvents` → `LootTableLoadEvent` / `GlobalLootModifierProvider`

**Recommended approach:** Move each file to `fabric/src/.../` as-is. When NeoForge support is needed, create a parallel file in `neoforge/src/.../` with the NeoForge event equivalents. No interface needed — these are pure side-effect registrations.

## Acceptance criteria

- None of the above files import `net.fabricmc.fabric.api.event.*`
- `common/` still compiles; Fabric behaviour is unchanged
- Each moved file is wired up in the appropriate Fabric entry point

## Overview

The `common/` subproject needs to become truly loader-agnostic so the `:neoforge` subproject can compile against it. This issue tracks all the work items needed to get there.

## Dependency order

Work flows in this order — each layer unblocks the next:

```
1. Pure moves (no abstraction needed)
   ├─ Move Fabric event registrations → fabric/
   ├─ Move capability lookup registrations → fabric/
   └─ Move packet .register() calls → fabric/

2. Vanilla substitutions
   ├─ Replace FabricBlockEntityTypeBuilder with vanilla
   └─ Move creative tab / biome registration → fabric/

3. Platform services (small, isolated)
   ├─ Platform.configDir() service
   └─ Resource reload listener abstraction

4. Energy abstraction  ← unblocks power domain + automation
   └─ IEnergyStorage contract + HasEnergyStorage update

5. Item storage abstraction  ← unblocks all pipe work (the big one)
   └─ IItemStorage / ITransaction contract + HasItemStorage update

6. Domain ports (parallelizable once 4 & 5 are done)
   ├─ Port pipe modules to IItemStorage
   ├─ Port pipe network to IItemStorage
   ├─ Port power domain to IEnergyStorage
   └─ Port automation domain
```

## Child issues

_Links will be added as issues are created._

## Acceptance criteria

- `:common` subproject has zero `net.fabricmc.*` and `team.reborn.*` imports
- `:neoforge` can compile against `:common` sources
- All existing game tests pass on Fabric after the refactor

This document defines how this repo will be structured and released once we support multiple Minecraft versions in parallel.

---

# 🎯 Goals

- Support **multiple Minecraft versions at once** without versioning chaos.
- Keep **stable releases** clean and automated via `release-please`.
- Keep **snapshot/testing builds** flowing without polluting stable releases.
- Allow **independent patching per MC line** (older versions can receive fixes without forcing new releases everywhere).

---

# 🧱 Branch Model

After MC 26.1 releases, the repo will follow this structure:

## Stable / maintenance branches
- `mc/1.21.11` → Maintenance branch for MC 1.21.11  
- `mc/26.1` → Maintenance branch for MC 26.1  

These branches:
- Receive bug fixes and approved backports
- Are the **only branches managed by release-please**
- Produce **stable releases**

## Forward development branch
- `main` → Development branch for **26.2 snapshots**

This branch:
- Tracks snapshots / next MC line
- Produces **test builds only**
- Does **not** use release-please

---

# 🔀 Cutover Plan (when MC 26.1 is released)

Current state assumption:
- `main` = current stable (1.21.11 era)
- `next` = work targeting 26.1

### Steps

1. Create `mc/1.21.11` from current `main`
2. Create `mc/26.1` from current `next`
3. Create new `main` from `mc/26.1`
4. Set new `main` as GitHub default branch

End state:

```
mc/1.21.11  → old stable line
mc/26.1     → new stable line
main        → 26.2 snapshot development
```

---

# 🚀 Release Model

## Stable releases (release-please)

- `release-please` runs on:  
  ```
  mc/**
  ```

- Each `mc/*` branch:
  - Has its **own independent version**
  - Maintains its own changelog + manifest
  - Cuts releases only when that line changes

### Tag safety (critical)

Each MC branch must use a **unique package name** in `release-please-config.json`.

Example:

On `mc/1.21.11`:
```json
"package-name": "logistics-mc1.21.11"
```

On `mc/26.1`:
```json
"package-name": "logistics-mc26.1"
```

With `include-component-in-tag: true`, tags become:

- `logistics-mc1.21.11-v0.2.6`
- `logistics-mc26.1-v0.3.1`

This prevents global git tag collisions and allows versions to diverge.

---

## Snapshot / testing builds (no release-please)

`main` publishes **snapshot builds only**, via CI.

Characteristics:
- Version includes `-snapshot` + SHA
- Published as **alpha** (or workflow artifacts only)
- No changelog PRs
- No GitHub Releases unless explicitly desired

Publishing options:
- manual (`workflow_dispatch`)
- on every push to `main`
- scheduled (nightly “latest snapshot”)

---

# 🔧 Backport Rules

### Default flow
1. Implement on `main`
2. Cherry-pick into:
   - `mc/26.1` if applicable
   - `mc/1.21.11` if still supported
3. Each branch releases independently

### Scenarios

#### Feature for all versions
- main → mc/26.1 → mc/1.21.11
- release from each branch

#### Bug only in 1.21.11
- fix only on `mc/1.21.11`
- release only from that branch

#### Bug in 26.1 and snapshots
- main → mc/26.1
- release only from `mc/26.1`

#### Critical bug everywhere
- main → all supported mc/*
- each branch releases

---

# 🧪 Snapshot Publishing Policy

Snapshots are:
- for testers
- allowed to be broken
- allowed to be spammy

Recommended early setup:
- manual publish workflow
- or push-to-main with alpha channel

Snapshots should:
- never update stable changelogs
- never block stable releases
- never reuse stable versions

---

# ✅ Validation Checklist (after setup)

- [ ] `mc/26.1` release produces tag like `logistics-mc26.1-vX.Y.Z`
- [ ] `mc/1.21.11` release produces different tag namespace
- [ ] Versions diverge safely
- [ ] Snapshot workflow builds from `main`
- [ ] Snapshot builds do not trigger release-please
- [ ] mc-publish handles multi-loader jars correctly

---

# 📌 Operating Principles

- Stable branches exist to **serve players**, not convenience.
- `main` exists to **move fast and break things**.
- Backports are intentional, not automatic.

payload.body:
## Summary

Currently, each pipe arm is implemented as **six separate baked models** (north/south/east/west/up/down) even though they are geometrically identical and only differ by orientation.

Now that all pipe rendering is handled in the **Block Entity Renderer (BER)** and we control the full transform pipeline, we can significantly simplify assets and maintenance by using **one base arm model** and rotating it to the correct direction at render time.

This will reduce model JSON count, simplify content creation, and make future pipe/module variants easier to maintain.

## Goals

- Replace 6 direction-specific arm models with **one base arm model**
- Rotate arms dynamically in the BER (or via rotated `BakedModel` wrappers)
- Preserve:
  - Correct world lighting
  - Nominal face directions for shading/AO
  - Compatibility with Sodium and modern rendering pipeline
- Keep performance acceptable (ideally bake/compute rotations once and cache)

## Context

- Pipes no longer use blockstate models.
- All pipe visuals are assembled dynamically in `PipeBlockEntityRenderer`.
- Arm models already **avoid `cullface`**, making them safe candidates for rotation.
- Current architecture already supports dynamic model selection via `Pipe.getArmModelId(...)`.

This task is a **rendering-layer improvement only**. Game logic and connection handling are unaffected.

## Proposed Implementation Options

### 🟢 Option A (Simple, fast, low risk)

Rotate the `MatrixStack` in the BER before submitting the arm model.

**How it works:**
- Keep a single arm model (e.g. `pipe_arm.json`, authored facing NORTH or EAST).
- For each connected direction:
  - `matrices.push()`
  - apply rotation based on `Direction`
  - `queue.submitModel(...)`
  - `matrices.pop()`

**Pros**
- Very easy to implement
- No custom model classes
- Immediate asset reduction

**Cons**
- Quad “nominal face” metadata is not rotated
- Can cause subtle lighting/AO inconsistencies (usually minor, especially since cullface is disabled)

This is likely “good enough” and may be all that’s ever needed.

### 🟡 Option B (Clean, technically correct, still one JSON)

Create **six rotated wrapper `BakedModel`s in code** from a single base model using Fabric Renderer API (FRAPI / Indigo).

**How it works:**
- Load one base arm `BakedModel`
- Create and cache six `RotatedArmModel` wrappers:
  - Each wrapper intercepts quad emission
  - Rotates vertex positions and normals
  - Remaps the quad’s nominal face (`NORTH → EAST`, etc.)
- BER selects the rotated wrapper instead of rotating matrices

**Pros**
- Correct face orientation for lighting/AO
- Still only one JSON model
- No per-frame math beyond normal rendering
- Clean long-term solution

**Cons**
- More complex to implement
- Requires FRAPI `FabricBakedModel` / `RenderContext` usage

**Implementation sketch:**
- Extend `ForwardingBakedModel implements FabricBakedModel`
- Override `emitBlockQuads(...)`
- `context.pushTransform(quad -> rotateQuad(quad, dir))`

## Recommended Path

1. Implement **Option A first** (matrix rotation).
2. If lighting artifacts appear or if correctness is desired long-term:
   - Upgrade to **Option B** with rotated baked wrappers.

Both approaches are compatible with the current architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Only **one arm model JSON** exists per pipe style
- [ ] Arms render correctly in all six directions
- [ ] Feature face overrides (modules) still work
- [ ] No face culling artifacts
- [ ] Lighting matches vanilla block behavior
- [ ] No regression to pipe rendering performance

## Notes

- Base arm model must be authored in a known orientation (recommend: **NORTH**).
- UP/DOWN arms will require X-axis rotations.
- Wrappers (Option B) should be cached, not rebuilt per frame.
- This task is independent of blockstate JSON cleanup.

payload.body:
## Problem

The mod currently experiences 36+ second initialization times due to a blockstate explosion.

**Current State:**
- Total blockstates: 183,708 (20,412 per pipe × 9 pipes)
- Calculation: 729 base states × 7 FEATURE_FACE values × 2 POWERED × 2 WATERLOGGED = 20,412 per pipe

## Root Cause

The `FEATURE_FACE` blockstate property (used to show the opaque extraction/output face on wooden and iron pipes) multiplies the number of blockstates by 7×. This property has 7 possible values (NONE, NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, WEST, UP, DOWN).

## Proposed Solution

Move `FEATURE_FACE` rendering to the Block Entity Renderer instead of using a blockstate property.

- Remove `FEATURE_FACE` from blockstate properties
- Render the opaque face texture in `PipeBlockEntityRenderer` based on module NBT data
- This approach is similar to how chest directions are rendered

## Expected Impact

**After fix:**
- Blockstates per pipe: 2,916 (729 base × 2 POWERED × 2 WATERLOGGED)
- Total blockstates: 26,244 (2,916 × 9 pipes)
- **85% reduction** in total blockstates
- Significantly faster initialization time

## Implementation Notes

- Affects `PipeBlock.java` - remove FEATURE_FACE property
- Affects `PipeBlockEntityRenderer.java` - add feature face rendering logic
- Affects `ExtractionModule.java` and `MergerModule.java` - change from blockstate to NBT-only storage
- May need to handle world upgrades (existing worlds with FEATURE_FACE in blockstates)

## Status

Deferred until after Minecraft 1.21.11 upgrade (now complete).
